submitter: bugfix_282_validate_accepts_menu lane (session bddf9352) — bugs_open/282, validate's resolver drops planner-placed tool sections — ROUND 2 (round 1 = REVISE, gated by editquality; 8 of 12 seats approved)
rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 returned REVISE. The gating seat (editquality) raised one HIGH plus three checkable objections; bug_historian raised a HIGH the router flagged as a scope question. All are answered below, and ONE CHANGED THE CODE — for the better, and beyond the caller I had scoped.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1 (commit adb1ee2ad, on top of 5534e9f71). bug_historian was right: accepting the menu restores acceptance for one opted-in caller and leaves the generic mechanism — resolve() dropping any unresolved name with a Warn and no durable trace — byte-identical to the bug being fixed. Any typo, renamed function, deleted component, or caller that never opts in still vanished silently. So EVERY drop now files a durable finding, for every caller, opted-in or not, through the door this action already uses for exactly this purpose (LogActionFindings/agenterrors — reuse, not new machinery; its own header states the standing reason that chassis logs rotate sub-second). Severity 'warning', matching recordRecomposeOutcomes in the same action: a drop IS a legal outcome (an unbuildable name must not reach site_plan_sections); what it must not be is invisible. The two cases carry DIFFERENT remedies because they are diagnostically different — with no menu_field the dropped name may be one the planner was legitimately OFFERED (282's own shape, so suspect the config before the name); with menu_field set it was in neither the base nor the menu, so it is a typo, a rename, or invention.

THE MUTATION PASS FOUND A REAL GAP IN MY OWN TESTS, TWICE, AND BOTH ARE FIXED. Mutation 'never collect a drop' PASSED against the first version — the tests asserted the findings' SHAPE and never the WIRING. Added a positive-assertion wiring test (the INSERT INTO agent_error_log must happen); it now fails under that mutation. Mutation 'delete the empty-drops guard' then ALSO passed, because a sqlmock CANNOT assert a negative: it fails an EXPECTED call that never came, never an UNEXPECTED call that did — so a recorder writing on every run satisfied the control. The recorder now RETURNS its attempted count, moving 'a clean plan writes nothing' somewhere a test can assert it; that test now fails under the mutation. Five mutations, all biting; 17 tests green; whole package suite green; clean-tree `git archive HEAD` build green.

THE FOUR CHECKABLE OBJECTIONS, ANSWERED BY QUERY RATHER THAN ASSERTION.
(1) editquality HIGH — 'the guard's jsonb path for output_field is unspecified; output_field can be nested in config'. Measured: `SELECT default_config#>>'{workflow,steps,load_components,output_field}'` returns 'available_components' and `#>>'{...,load_components,config,output_field}'` returns NULL — output_field is TOP-LEVEL in the step, which is the path 439 reads. Stronger evidence than the query: the migration is APPLIED and its DO-block guard passed, and that guard RAISEs when menu_source IS DISTINCT FROM menu_field — a wrong depth would have read NULL and aborted the apply.
(2) editquality + debug_historian MEDIUM — 'duplicate active rows; the UPDATE may hit the wrong one'. Measured: exactly ONE active non-snapshot build-site-planner row (version 1). The migration's own guard asserts count(*)=1 and RAISEs otherwise, so the landmine is checked at apply time regardless.
(3) editquality MEDIUM — 'config["menu_field"].(string) may be resolved as a REFERENCE not a literal'. ValidateSitePlanAction reads params.StepConfig.Config as a RAW MAP for every key it has (plan_field, max_pages, validate_components, default_style) and has NO RegisterActionInputSpec, so no input-resolution layer ever sees menu_field. The action-level tests pass the literal through that exact path end to end.
(4) editquality LOW — 'the test expects a component_level = site query the diagnosis never mentions'. Correct observation, and the test is right: ValidateSitePlanAction runs loadSiteChromeNames (component_level='site', the chrome strip) BEFORE the resolver's section/element query. Two queries, both real; round 1's diagnosis text simply did not mention the first.

PRIOR_ART_LIBRARIAN'S EVIDENTIARY OBJECTIONS, ACCEPTED AND CORRECTED. (a) The seat is right that my round-1 phrasing implied filtering orchestration_states by `agent_type`, a column this estate's own landmine says does not exist; the real column is `owner_agent_type`, and re-run correctly: site-planner returns ZERO rows. One nuance I should state rather than let stand: build-site-planner's own 2 rows have since aged out of that table, so '0 rows' is a claim about a RETENTION WINDOW, not about all history — the load-bearing part of leaving site-planner alone is not its dormancy but that its menu is section/element-only, so opting it in would add nothing. (b) content-gap-planner has NO validate_site_plan step — queried, not assumed: only build-site-planner.validate_plan and site-planner.validate_plan carry that action. (c) The four-caller claim: `grep -rn loadComponentNameResolver` returns v3_site_actions.go:3411 plus apply_gap_plan_action.go:230/362/890. (d) The zero-test-coverage claim rests on a grep over *_test.go source files (not the code index, whose declaration-only limitation the seat correctly cites) — and it is now moot, since this change adds the coverage either way.

REUSE_AGENT / TOOLING_PROVENANCE (both approved, cheap asks honoured). The residual-drop recorder deliberately reuses LogActionFindings rather than minting a second reporting path. The reasoning is carried forward in durable form — concept register PLAN-050 (new) with PLAN-027 amended and PLAN-049 given the back-relation it never had, plus a LANDMINES entry (synced to doc_notes, verifier dispatched) and a 016b §10 row — so the next fixer on this seam does not re-derive it from a bug file that may be archived.

GUARDIAN (approved, containment asks). The v3_site_actions.go hunks are minimal and landed cleanly with no same-file passenger (verified by diff before commit); the sub_workflow blind spot is checked — the validate_site_plan enumeration above scans every step of every live agent, and no nested sub_workflow carries it.

UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1: the core mechanism, and every reason for it. The menu is a SQL string in agent_definitions that had already drifted (419 edited 407's query and guards its apply on 407's exact bytes), so the acceptance surface consumes the offer's OUTPUT rather than re-deriving its predicate; UNION never removal; opt-in with the unsafe default OFF; the shared resolver's query and signature untouched so apply_gap_plan's three call sites keep the authority PLAN-049 withheld from them; order-safe in both deploy directions.

plan.summary: ROUND 2. As round 1 (validate_site_plan gains an opt-in `menu_field` naming the collected-data path holding the component menu its own planner step was shown; those rows are UNIONed into the name resolver) PLUS the council's gating fix: every dropped section name now files a durable finding via the action's existing LogActionFindings door, for every caller opted-in or not, so the silent-loss mechanism is closed as a CLASS rather than for one caller. Migration 439 (applied) opts in build-site-planner only.

edits.rationale: New file, not a hunk in v3_site_actions.go: that file is edited by several sessions concurrently (it was dirty from another lane this morning) and a same-file passenger cannot be prevented by any pathspec. addMenu UNIONs menu rows into validFunctions/nameToFunc/displayToFunc with the DB base winning on identity collisions; menuRowsFrom refuses anything that is not a non-empty []interface{} so a misconfigured path degrades to today's behaviour rather than to a resolver that accepts ""; resolvedViaMenu exists so a run can SAY the arm fired.

Two minimal hunks. The struct gains menuOnly (attribution only). The call site reads the opt-in key and logs both the arm firing and, per resolved section, whether it owes acceptance to the menu — without that tell, 'the widening reached the plan' and 'the planner proposed nothing from the widened class' are indistinguishable in the logs and in site_plan_sections.

407's idiom: snapshot_agent, jsonb_set, DO-block guard that RAISEs. The guard checks BOTH halves together — menu_field must equal load_components.output_field — because a menu_field naming a path no step writes is the one way this change can be inert while looking applied, which is bugs_open/282 itself one level up. ROLLBACK sidecar removes the key, which is a complete revert whether or not the Go has rolled.

The resolver had ZERO test coverage before this (grep of *_test.go for loadComponentNameResolver: no hits), which is part of why a whole class of names could vanish unnoticed. Nine tests: menu function resolves and is attributed; display-name echo resolves; base identity wins a collision; malformed rows add nothing and never make "" valid; shape variance on the collected-data path; and two sqlmock action-level tests — WITH menu_field the tool section survives, WITHOUT it the identical plan still drops it (the un-opted-in control).

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, answering bug_historian's HIGH. A drop was previously a Warn and nothing else — the estate's most-repeated failure shape (content silently lost in a plan pass, discovered only after damage). Now every drop files a durable agenterrors Finding through LogActionFindings, the door this action already uses for recordRecomposeOutcomes, with the same 'warning' severity and the same reasoning (a drop is a legal outcome; invisibility is not). Applies to EVERY caller, including the un-opted-in ones the scoping decision leaves on the old behaviour, so their exposure is now visible rather than implied. droppedRemedy/droppedFindings are pure so the record's shape is assertable without a database; recordDroppedSectionNames returns its attempted count because a mock cannot prove the negative case.
